concepts.name: French nasal vowels
concepts.summary: Recognise and pronounce the nasal vowels /ɑ̃/, /ɔ̃/ and /ɛ̃/ without sounding a final n or m, as in blanc, bon and vin.

concepts.name: Silent final letters
concepts.summary: Understand that most final consonants and the final e are not pronounced, as in petit, grand and parle, and apply this when reading aloud.

concepts.name: Accents and cedilla
concepts.summary: Remember the acute, grave, circumflex and cedilla marks and what sound each signals, such as é versus è and soft ç.

concepts.name: Uvular French r
concepts.summary: Understand and produce the French r at the back of the throat rather than a rolled or English r.

concepts.name: Definite and indefinite articles
concepts.summary: Choose le, la, l' or les and un, une or des according to the noun's gender and number.

concepts.name: Être and avoir present
concepts.summary: Recall and understand the present-tense forms of être and avoir and use them in simple statements about identity and possession.

concepts.name: Greetings and tu vs vous
concepts.summary: Understand when to use informal tu and formal or plural vous in basic greetings and introductions.

misconceptions.text: The final n or m in a nasal vowel is pronounced as a separate consonant.
Accents on French letters are optional decoration that do not change pronunciation or meaning.
The French r should be rolled with the tip of the tongue like in Spanish.

concepts.name: Liaison rules
concepts.summary: Apply obligatory liaison, as in les amis and vous avez, and avoid it in forbidden contexts such as after et.

concepts.name: Partitive articles
concepts.summary: Use du, de la, de l' for unspecified quantities of food and abstractions, and switch to de after negation.

concepts.name: Regular present tense verbs
concepts.summary: Conjugate regular -er, -ir and -re verbs in the present tense and use them in everyday sentences.

concepts.name: Adjective agreement and position
concepts.summary: Make adjectives agree in gender and number and place them correctly, including the common pre-noun adjectives.

concepts.name: Negation with ne pas
concepts.summary: Form negative sentences by wrapping ne around the verb with pas, using n' before vowels.

concepts.name: Passé composé formation
concepts.summary: Form the passé composé with avoir or être and a past participle to report completed actions.

concepts.name: Question formation
concepts.summary: Ask yes/no and information questions using intonation, est-ce que and question words.

misconceptions.text: Partitive articles stay du or de la after a negation.
All past participles are formed by simply adding é to the infinitive stem.
Adjectives always follow the noun as in Spanish.

concepts.name: Imparfait formation and use
concepts.summary: Form the imparfait from the nous stem and use it for habits, descriptions and ongoing states in the past.

concepts.name: Passé composé versus imparfait
concepts.summary: Analyse a narrative to decide whether each verb is a completed event (passé composé) or background/habitual (imparfait).

concepts.name: Auxiliary choice and agreement
concepts.summary: Distinguish verbs taking être, including reflexives, and apply participle agreement with the subject or a preceding direct object.

concepts.name: Object and adverbial pronouns
concepts.summary: Replace direct and indirect objects and places or quantities with le, lui, y and en in the correct position.

concepts.name: Register and politeness choice
concepts.summary: Analyse social context to choose tu or vous and adapt vocabulary and phrasing between familiar and formal registers.

concepts.name: Future and conditional forms
concepts.summary: Form and use the futur simple, futur proche and present conditional for plans, predictions and polite requests.

concepts.name: DELF A2-B1 task formats
concepts.summary: Apply strategies to the four DELF skills at A2 to B1, including listening, reading, structured writing and interview.

misconceptions.text: The imparfait is simply the French equivalent of one English past tense and can replace the passé composé whenever the action is old.
Every past participle agrees with the subject.
Vous is always the safe choice, so tu never needs to be learned or used with peers.

concepts.name: Subjunctive mood triggers
concepts.summary: Analyse which expressions of necessity, emotion, doubt and wish require the subjunctive and form it correctly.

concepts.name: Pluperfect and sequence of tenses
concepts.summary: Use the plus-que-parfait and conditional perfect to sequence events and build si-clauses across time frames.

concepts.name: Relative pronouns complex
concepts.summary: Select qui, que, dont, où and lequel forms according to the grammatical function in the relative clause.

concepts.name: Discourse connectors and nuance
concepts.summary: Judge which connectors such as cependant, néanmoins and en revanche best express the intended logical relation.

concepts.name: Argumentative writing structure
concepts.summary: Evaluate and structure an argument with thesis, connectors, counterpoints and conclusion for DELF B2 writing.

concepts.name: Passive and nominalisation
concepts.summary: Transform active constructions into passive or nominal forms to achieve a more formal, impersonal style.

concepts.name: DELF B2 exam strategy
concepts.summary: Evaluate own performance against DELF B2 criteria and refine timing and strategy for each exam component.

misconceptions.text: The subjunctive is used whenever the main clause is in a certain tense or whenever que appears.
Si can be followed by the conditional in any si-clause.
Connectors like pourtant, donc and cependant are interchangeable in a written argument.

concepts.name: Literary tenses recognition
concepts.summary: Evaluate the stylistic effect of the passé simple and imperfect subjunctive when interpreting literary and formal texts.

concepts.name: Stylistic register manipulation
concepts.summary: Create texts that deliberately shift register, from argot and familier to soutenu, for rhetorical effect.

concepts.name: Synthesis writing for DALF C1
concepts.summary: Produce a coherent synthesis combining several source documents and a reasoned argumentative essay at C1 level.

concepts.name: Oral argumentation DALF C1-C2
concepts.summary: Construct and defend a structured oral presentation and respond to challenge with spontaneous, precise language.

concepts.name: Idiom and figurative language
concepts.summary: Judge the appropriateness of idioms, proverbs and figures of speech in context and across regional varieties.

concepts.name: Phonetic variation and prosody
concepts.summary: Evaluate regional and social pronunciation variation, including optional liaison and schwa deletion, and control prosody.

concepts.name: DALF C2 critical commentary
concepts.summary: Design and deliver a nuanced critical commentary on complex texts that meets DALF C2 expectations of precision and fluency.

misconceptions.text: Literary tenses like the passé simple should be used in everyday speech to sound advanced.
A DALF synthesis should include the writer's own opinion on the sources.
There is one correct standard pronunciation, and liaison is always pronounced in careful speech.
